571	def _tag_constraints_compatible(r1, r2, tp1, tp2, te1, te2):
572	    """True iff one tag assignment can satisfy both rules' constraints.
573	
574	    ``tp1``/``tp2`` are the rules' ``tag_patterns`` values compiled by
575	    :func:`_tokenize_pattern`; ``te1``/``te2`` are their compiled
576	    ``tag_exclude_patterns``. Constraints on disjoint keys are jointly
577	    satisfiable (the caller may supply extra tags). On a shared key, two
578	    exact values conflict only when unequal, an exact value must match
579	    the pattern, and two patterns need one common string. A pattern
580	    matching no string at all makes its own rule unsatisfiable, so no
581	    request can match both rules. Exclusion constraints further require
582	    the key's value to avoid every ``tag_exclude_patterns`` pattern
583	    declared for it by either rule: an exact value fails when it is a
584	    string hitting an exclusion pattern, and a pattern- or
585	    exclusion-only key needs one string that satisfies its positive
586	    patterns (if any) while matching none of the exclusion patterns.
587	    Presence constraints only look at the key: one rule requiring a key
588	    the other rule forbids is unsatisfiable, and a key either rule
589	    forbids must not be forced present by the other rule's exact or
590	    pattern constraints (an exclusion alone never forces presence, so a
591	    forbidden key simply stays absent and passes every exclusion).
592	    """
593	    tags1, pats1 = r1["tags"], r1["tag_patterns"]
594	    tags2, pats2 = r2["tags"], r2["tag_patterns"]
595	    pres1, pres2 = r1["tag_presence"], r2["tag_presence"]
596	    forbidden = set()
597	    for key, required in pres1.items():
598	        if key in pres2 and pres2[key] != required:
599	            return False
600	        if not required:
601	            forbidden.add(key)
602	    for key, required in pres2.items():
603	        if not required:
604	            forbidden.add(key)
605	    for key in forbidden:
606	        if key in tags1 or key in tags2 or key in pats1 or key in pats2:
607	            return False
608	    for tokens in tp1.values():
609	        if not _pattern_satisfiable(tokens):
610	            return False
611	    for tokens in tp2.values():
612	        if not _pattern_satisfiable(tokens):
613	            return False
614	    for key, value in tags1.items():
615	        if key in tags2:
616	            if tags2[key] != value:
617	                return False
618	        elif key in pats2 and not _value_matches_pattern(value, pats2[key]):
619	            return False
620	    for key, value in tags2.items():
621	        if key in pats1 and not _value_matches_pattern(value, pats1[key]):
622	            return False
623	    for key in pats1:
624	        if key in pats2 and not _patterns_overlap(tp1[key], tp2[key]):
625	            return False
626	    for key in set(te1) | set(te2):
627	        if key in forbidden:
628	            # The key stays absent, which passes every exclusion.
629	            continue
630	        if key in tags1 or key in tags2:
631	            value = tags1[key] if key in tags1 else tags2[key]
632	            for rule in (r1, r2):
633	                pattern = rule["tag_exclude_patterns"].get(key)
634	                if pattern is not None and _value_matches_pattern(
635	                    value, pattern
636	                ):
637	                    return False
638	        else:
639	            positives = []
640	            if key in pats1:
641	                positives.append(tp1[key])
642	            if key in pats2:
643	                positives.append(tp2[key])
644	            negatives = []
645	            if key in te1:
646	                negatives.append(te1[key])
647	            if key in te2:
648	                negatives.append(te2[key])
649	            if _min_string_avoiding(positives, negatives) is None:
650	                return False
651	    return True

654	def _witness_tags(r1, r2, tp1, tp2, te1, te2):
655	    """Joint tag assignment satisfying both rules' tag constraints.
656	
657	    Only keys constrained by one of the two rules appear — whether in
658	    ``tags``, ``tag_patterns``, ``tag_exclude_patterns`` or
659	    ``tag_presence`` — emitted in Unicode code-point order. An exact
660	    constraint pins the value (a shared exact/pattern key takes the
661	    exact value, which the compatibility check has already proven to
662	    match every positive pattern and avoid every exclusion); a key
663	    constrained only by patterns and exclusions takes the shortest
664	    string satisfying every positive pattern on it and matching none of
665	    its exclusion patterns, ties broken by Unicode code-point
666	    lexicographic order. A key either rule's ``tag_presence`` forbids
667	    is never written (its absence satisfies every exclusion on it); a
668	    key only required to exist, with no exact, pattern or exclusion
669	    constraint from either rule, takes the shortest string satisfying
670	    both sides' conditions — the empty string. Exact values
671	    are deep-copied (direct construction permits mutable tag values) so
672	    a caller mutating a returned report can never touch the loaded rules
673	    or later reports.
674	    """
675	    keys = (
676	        set(r1["tags"])
677	        | set(r1["tag_patterns"])
678	        | set(r1["tag_exclude_patterns"])
679	        | set(r1["tag_presence"])
680	        | set(r2["tags"])
681	        | set(r2["tag_patterns"])
682	        | set(r2["tag_exclude_patterns"])
683	        | set(r2["tag_presence"])
684	    )
685	    forbidden = {
686	        key
687	        for rule in (r1, r2)
688	        for key, required in rule["tag_presence"].items()
689	        if not required
690	    }
691	    merged = {}
692	    for key in keys:
693	        if key in forbidden:
694	            continue
695	        exact = None
696	        have_exact = False
697	        patterns = []
698	        negatives = []
699	        for rule, compiled, excluded in ((r1, tp1, te1), (r2, tp2, te2)):
700	            if key in rule["tags"]:
701	                have_exact = True
702	                exact = rule["tags"][key]
703	            elif key in rule["tag_patterns"]:
704	                patterns.append(compiled[key])
705	            if key in rule["tag_exclude_patterns"]:
706	                negatives.append(excluded[key])
707	        if have_exact:
708	            merged[key] = copy.deepcopy(exact)
709	        elif negatives:
710	            merged[key] = _min_string_avoiding(patterns, negatives)
711	        elif len(patterns) == 1:
712	            merged[key] = _min_pattern_string(patterns[0])
713	        elif patterns:
714	            merged[key] = _min_common_string(patterns[0], patterns[1])
715	        else:
716	            # Presence-only key: the shortest string is the empty one.
717	            merged[key] = ""
718	    return {key: merged[key] for key in sorted(merged)}

721	def _pair_witness(r1, r2, c1, c2):
722	    """Minimum request matching both selectors of one audited pair."""
723	    return {
724	        "subject": _min_common_string(c1[0], c2[0]),
725	        "action": _min_common_string(c1[1], c2[1]),
726	        "resource": _min_common_string(c1[2], c2[2]),
727	        "tags": _witness_tags(r1, r2, c1[3], c2[3], c1[4], c2[4]),

731	def _patterns_overlap(t1, t2):
732	    """True iff some string matches both tokenized glob patterns.
733	
734	    Dynamic programming over the token grid: dp[i][j] is True when the
735	    suffixes t1[i:] and t2[j:] can match a common string. `*` either
736	    matches empty or absorbs one character matched by the other side.
737	    """
738	    n1, n2 = len(t1), len(t2)
739	    star1 = [True] * (n1 + 1)
740	    for i in range(n1 - 1, -1, -1):
741	        star1[i] = star1[i + 1] and t1[i][0] == "star"
742	    star2 = [True] * (n2 + 1)
743	    for j in range(n2 - 1, -1, -1):
744	        star2[j] = star2[j + 1] and t2[j][0] == "star"
745	
746	    row = bytearray(star2)  # row i == n1: t1 exhausted, t2[j:] must be stars
747	    for i in range(n1 - 1, -1, -1):
748	        cur = bytearray(n2 + 1)
749	        cur[n2] = star1[i]
750	        a = t1[i]
751	        a_star = a[0] == "star"
752	        for j in range(n2 - 1, -1, -1):
753	            b = t2[j]
754	            if a_star and b[0] == "star":
755	                cur[j] = cur[j + 1] or row[j]
756	            elif a_star:
757	                cur[j] = row[j] or (_class_satisfiable(b) and cur[j + 1])
758	            elif b[0] == "star":
759	                cur[j] = cur[j + 1] or (_class_satisfiable(a) and row[j])
760	            else:
761	                cur[j] = _classes_overlap(a, b) and row[j + 1]
762	        row = cur
763	    return bool(row[0])

766	def _audit_pair(r1, r2, c1, c2):
767	    """Build the finding for one rule pair, or None when there is none."""
768	    if not (
769	        _patterns_overlap(c1[0], c2[0])
770	        and _patterns_overlap(c1[1], c2[1])
771	        and _patterns_overlap(c1[2], c2[2])
772	        and _tag_constraints_compatible(r1, r2, c1[3], c2[3], c1[4], c2[4])
773	    ):
774	        return None
775	
776	    identical = (
777	        r1["subject"] == r2["subject"]
778	        and r1["action"] == r2["action"]
779	        and r1["resource"] == r2["resource"]
780	        and r1["tags"] == r2["tags"]
781	        and r1["tag_patterns"] == r2["tag_patterns"]
782	        and r1["tag_exclude_patterns"] == r2["tag_exclude_patterns"]
783	        and r1["tag_presence"] == r2["tag_presence"]
784	    )
785	    if identical:
786	        # Identical selectors: one rule can never win, so it is shadowed.
787	        if r1["effect"] != r2["effect"]:
788	            winner = r1 if r1["effect"] == "deny" else r2
789	            severity = "error"
790	        else:
791	            # r1 is declared earlier, so it wins priority ties.
792	            winner = r1 if r1["priority"] >= r2["priority"] else r2
793	            severity = "warning"
794	        loser = r2 if winner is r1 else r1
795	        if severity == "error":
796	            reason = (
797	                "rule %r is fully shadowed by deny rule %r: identical "
798	                "selectors, and explicit deny overrides allow"
799	                % (loser["id"], winner["id"])
800	            )
801	        else:
802	            reason = (
803	                "rule %r is fully shadowed by rule %r: identical "
804	                "selectors, and priority then declaration order always "
805	                "prefer %r" % (loser["id"], winner["id"], winner["id"])
806	            )
807	        return {
808	            "code": "shadowed_rule",
809	            "severity": severity,
810	            "rule": r1["id"],
811	            "other_rule": r2["id"],
812	            "winner": winner["id"],
813	            "shadowed": loser["id"],
814	            "reason": reason,
815	            "witness": _pair_witness(r1, r2, c1, c2),
816	        }
817	
818	    if r1["effect"] != r2["effect"]:
819	        deny = r1 if r1["effect"] == "deny" else r2
820	        allow = r2 if deny is r1 else r1
821	        return {
822	            "code": "effect_overlap",
823	            "severity": "error",
824	            "rule": r1["id"],
825	            "other_rule": r2["id"],
826	            "winner": deny["id"],
827	            "shadowed": None,
828	            "reason": (
829	                "selectors overlap; explicit deny rule %r overrides allow "
830	                "rule %r for every request matching both, regardless of "
831	                "priority" % (deny["id"], allow["id"])
832	            ),
833	            "witness": _pair_witness(r1, r2, c1, c2),
834	        }
835	
836	    # Same-effect partial overlap is not a conflict.
837	    return None

872	            if not isinstance(priority, int) or isinstance(priority, bool):

921	                    "keys and string pattern values" % i
922	                )

1020	                "root_not_array",

1113	    @staticmethod
1114	    def _tags_match(rule, tags):
1115	        # Exact constraints compare values for equality; pattern
1116	        # constraints apply fnmatch.fnmatchcase to the request's tag
1117	        # value, so a missing key or a non-string value simply means the
1118	        # rule does not match. Exclusion constraints invert the pattern
1119	        # test: a missing key, a non-string value or a value that does
1120	        # not match the exclusion pattern all pass, and only an actual
1121	        # hit makes the rule not match. Presence constraints only look at
1122	        # the key: a ``True`` entry demands the key exist (its value may
1123	        # be of any type), a ``False`` entry demands it be absent.
1124	        return (
1125	            all(tags.get(k) == v for k, v in rule["tags"].items())
1126	            and all(
1127	                _value_matches_pattern(tags.get(k), pattern)
1128	                for k, pattern in rule["tag_patterns"].items()
1129	            )
1130	            and all(
1131	                not _value_matches_pattern(tags.get(k), pattern)
1132	                for k, pattern in rule["tag_exclude_patterns"].items()
1133	            )
1134	            and all(
1135	                (k in tags) == required
1136	                for k, required in rule["tag_presence"].items()
1137	            )
1138	        )

1142	        return (
1143	            fnmatch.fnmatchcase(subject, rule["subject"])
1144	            and fnmatch.fnmatchcase(action, rule["action"])
1145	            and fnmatch.fnmatchcase(resource, rule["resource"])
1146	            and PolicyGate._tags_match(rule, tags)
1147	        )

1149	    @staticmethod
1150	    def _check_inputs(subject, action, resource, tags):
1151	        for name, value in (
1152	            ("subject", subject),
1153	            ("action", action),
1154	            ("resource", resource),
1155	        ):
1156	            if not isinstance(value, str):
1157	                raise TypeError("%s must be a string" % name)

1160	        elif not isinstance(tags, Mapping):

1164	    @staticmethod
1165	    def _select(matched):
1166	        """Pick the winning rule out of the matched ones.
1167	
1168	        Explicit deny always wins; within one effect, higher priority wins,
1169	        then the earliest declaration order breaks ties deterministically.
1170	        Returns (decision, winner rule or None).
1171	        """
1172	        denies = [r for r in matched if r["effect"] == "deny"]
1173	        allows = [r for r in matched if r["effect"] == "allow"]
1174	
1175	        winners = denies if denies else allows
1176	        if not winners:
1177	            return (
1178	                {"effect": "deny", "rule": None, "reason": "default deny"},
1179	                None,
1180	            )
1181	
1182	        winner = min(winners, key=lambda r: (-r["priority"], r["_index"]))
1183	        reason = "matched %s rule %r (priority %d)" % (
1184	            winner["effect"],
1185	            winner["id"],
1186	            winner["priority"],
1187	        )
1188	        if winner["effect"] == "deny" and allows:
1189	            reason += "; explicit deny overrides allow"
1190	        return (
1191	            {"effect": winner["effect"], "rule": winner["id"], "reason": reason},
1192	            winner,
1193	        )

1195	    def _evaluate(self, subject, action, resource, tags):
1196	        """Shared decision core; returns (decision, matched rules in order)."""
1197	        tags = self._check_inputs(subject, action, resource, tags)
1198	
1199	        matched = [
1200	            r
1201	            for r in self.rules
1202	            if self._matches(r, subject, action, resource, tags)
1203	        ]
1204	        decision, _winner = self._select(matched)
1205	        return decision, matched

1207	    def decide(self, subject, action, resource, tags=None):
1208	        result, _matched = self._evaluate(subject, action, resource, tags)
1209	        return result

1330	    def decide_many(self, requests):
1331	        """Evaluate many requests in one offline, reviewable batch.
1332	
1333	        ``requests`` must be a list or tuple of mappings, each limited to
1334	        the keys ``subject``, ``action``, ``resource`` and ``tags``. The
1335	        first three are required strings; ``tags`` may be omitted, be
1336	        ``None`` or be any mapping accepted by :meth:`decide`.
1337	
1338	        Returns ``{"decisions": [...], "summary": {"total", "allow",
1339	        "deny"}}`` with decisions in input order, each identical to what a
1340	        plain :meth:`decide` call would return. An empty batch yields an
1341	        empty decision list and an all-zero summary.
1342

1344	        malformed batch raises :class:`PolicyBatchError` and never produces
1345	        partial results. Rules and caller data are never modified.
1346	        """
1347	        self._validate_requests(requests)
1348	
1349	        decisions = [
1350	            self.decide(
1351	                item["subject"],
1352	                item["action"],
1353	                item["resource"],
1354	                item.get("tags"),
1355	            )
1356	            for item in requests
1357	        ]
1358	        summary = {
1359	            "total": len(decisions),
1360	            "allow": sum(1 for d in decisions if d["effect"] == "allow"),
1361	            "deny": sum(1 for d in decisions if d["effect"] == "deny"),
1362	        }

1365	    def verify(self, cases):
1366	        """Check fixed cases against the rules before a release.
1367	
1368	        ``cases`` must be a list or tuple of mappings, each limited to the
1369	        keys ``subject``, ``action``, ``resource``, ``tags`` and
1370	        ``expected``. The first three are required strings with the same
1371	        meaning as in :meth:`decide`; ``tags`` may be omitted, be ``None``
1372	        or be any mapping accepted by :meth:`decide`. ``expected`` is
1373	        required and must be a mapping holding exactly ``effect``
1374	        (``"allow"`` or ``"deny"``) and ``rule`` (a string or ``None``;
1375	        the default deny is written as ``{"effect": "deny", "rule": None}``).
1376	
1377	        The whole batch is validated before any decision is computed, so a
1378	        malformed batch raises :class:`PolicyVerificationError` and never
1379	        produces partial results. Its ``code``/``index``/``field`` follow
1380	        the error-class order: ``invalid_cases`` for a non-list/tuple
1381	        batch, ``item_not_mapping`` for a non-mapping element,
1382	        ``unknown_field`` / ``missing_field`` / ``invalid_field_type`` for
1383	        case fields (nested expectation fields are reported as
1384	        ``expected.effect`` / ``expected.rule``), and
1385	        ``invalid_expectation`` for an illegal ``expected`` value.
1386	
1387	        After validation, cases are evaluated in input order using the
1388	        existing :meth:`decide` semantics (glob matching, exact, pattern
1389	        and exclusion tag constraints, explicit deny, priority,
1390	        declaration order and
1391	        default deny). A case passes only when both ``effect`` and
1392	        ``rule`` equal the actual decision; ``reason`` never participates.
1393	
1394	        Returns ``{"ok", "failures", "summary"}`` — namely the fixed keys
1395	        ``ok``, ``failures`` and ``summary`` — where ``summary`` holds
1396	        ``total``, ``passed`` and ``failed``. Each failure is listed in
1397	        input order as ``{"index", "expected", "actual"}`` with ``actual``
1398	        the complete :meth:`decide` result; ``ok`` is true exactly when
1399	        ``failed`` is zero. An empty batch yields an empty failure list,
1400	        an all-zero summary and ``ok`` true. Returned mappings are
1401	        independent copies, so mutating a report never affects later
1402	        calls. Verification is read-only and offline: rules and inputs
1403	        are never modified, no I/O happens, and gates built directly and
1404	        via :meth:`from_json` verify identically.
1405	        """
1406	        self._validate_cases(cases)
1407	
1408	        failures = []
1409	        passed = 0
1410	        for index, item in enumerate(cases):
1411	            actual = self.decide(
1412	                item["subject"],
1413	                item["action"],
1414	                item["resource"],
1415	                item.get("tags"),
1416	            )
1417	            expected = item["expected"]
1418	            if (
1419	                actual["effect"] == expected["effect"]
1420	                and actual["rule"] == expected["rule"]
1421	            ):
1422	                passed += 1
1423	            else:
1424	                failures.append(
1425	                    {
1426	                        "index": index,
1427	                        "expected": copy.deepcopy(expected),
1428	                        "actual": copy.deepcopy(actual),
1429	                    }
1430	                )
1431	
1432	        total = len(cases)
1433	        return {
1434	            "ok": passed == total,
1435	            "failures": failures,
1436	            "summary": {"total": total, "passed": passed,
1437	                        "failed": total - passed},
1438	        }

1440	    def coverage(self, requests):
1441	        """Measure how the loaded rules participate in deciding a batch.
1442	
1443	        ``requests`` uses the same list/tuple of request mappings as
1444	        :meth:`decide_many` and is validated exactly the same way: the
1445	        whole batch is checked first, and a malformed batch raises
1446	        :class:`PolicyBatchError` with ``code``/``index``/``field``
1447	        instead of producing a partial report.
1448	
1449	        Returns ``{"rules": [...], "summary": {...}}``. ``rules`` lists
1450	        every loaded rule in declaration order as ``{"id", "effect",
1451	        "matched", "winner"}``: ``matched`` counts the requests whose
1452	        subject/action/resource matched the rule's glob patterns under
1453	        ``fnmatch.fnmatchcase`` semantics together with its exact,
1454	        pattern and exclusion tag constraints, and ``winner`` counts the
1455	        requests the rule
1456	        actually decided after explicit-deny precedence, priority and
1457	        declaration-order tie-breaking. A request matching several rules
1458	        raises every matched rule's ``matched`` but only the final
1459	        rule's ``winner``; a request falling through to the default deny
1460	        raises no rule's ``winner``.
1461	
1462	        ``summary`` has the fixed keys ``total``, ``allow``,
1463	        ``explicit_deny``, ``default_deny`` and ``matched_request``:
1464	        ``allow`` counts requests whose final effect is allow,
1465	        ``explicit_deny`` counts requests won by a deny rule,
1466	        ``default_deny`` counts requests that matched no rule at all,
1467	        and ``matched_request`` counts requests matching at least one
1468	        rule. An empty batch yields all-zero counts; with an empty rule
1469	        set every request lands in ``default_deny``.
1470	
1471	        The report is read-only and offline: rules and caller mappings
1472	        are never modified, no I/O happens, and repeated calls over the
1473	        same batch return equal results.
1474	        """
1475	        self._validate_requests(requests)
1476	
1477	        matched_counts = [0] * len(self.rules)
1478	        winner_counts = [0] * len(self.rules)
1479	        index_by_id = {r["id"]: r["_index"] for r in self.rules}
1480	        allow = explicit_deny = default_deny = matched_request = 0
1481	
1482	        for item in requests:
1483	            decision, matched = self._evaluate(
1484	                item["subject"],
1485	                item["action"],
1486	                item["resource"],
1487	                item.get("tags"),
1488	            )
1489	            for rule in matched:
1490	                matched_counts[rule["_index"]] += 1
1491	            if matched:
1492	                matched_request += 1
1493	            if decision["rule"] is None:
1494	                default_deny += 1
1495	            else:
1496	                winner_counts[index_by_id[decision["rule"]]] += 1
1497	                if decision["effect"] == "allow":
1498	                    allow += 1
1499	                else:
1500	                    explicit_deny += 1
1501	
1502	        rules = [
1503	            {
1504	                "id": rule["id"],
1505	                "effect": rule["effect"],
1506	                "matched": matched_counts[rule["_index"]],
1507	                "winner": winner_counts[rule["_index"]],
1508	            }
1509	            for rule in self.rules
1510	        ]
1511	        summary = {
1512	            "total": len(requests),
1513	            "allow": allow,
1514	            "explicit_deny": explicit_deny,
1515	            "default_deny": default_deny,
1516	            "matched_request": matched_request,
1517	        }
1518	        return {"rules": rules, "summary": summary}

1520	    def compare(self, candidate, requests):
1521	        """Compare this gate (the baseline) against ``candidate`` on one batch.
1522	
1523	        The two gates each apply their own glob matching, explicit-deny,
1524	        priority, declaration-order and default-deny rules to the same
1525	        requests; the point of the comparison is to locate exactly what a
1526	        candidate policy change alters.
1527	
1528	        ``candidate`` must be a :class:`PolicyGate`, otherwise ``TypeError``
1529	        is raised. ``requests`` uses the same list/tuple of request
1530	        mappings as :meth:`decide_many` and is validated exactly the same
1531	        way (:class:`PolicyBatchError` with ``code``/``index``/``field``;
1532	        the first error aborts the whole comparison with no partial
1533	        results). Validation of ``candidate`` and the whole batch finishes
1534	        before either gate evaluates anything. An empty batch returns an
1535	        all-zero summary and no changes.
1536	
1537	        Returns ``{"changes": [...], "summary": {"total", "unchanged",
1538	        "changed", "allow_to_deny", "deny_to_allow", "winner_changed"}}``.
1539	        ``total`` is the request count; each change is listed in input
1540	        order as ``{"index", "before", "after", "kind"}``, where
1541	        ``before``/``after`` are the full :meth:`decide` results of the
1542	        baseline and the candidate. ``kind`` is ``allow_to_deny`` or
1543	        ``deny_to_allow`` when the effect flips, and ``winner_changed``
1544	        when the effect is the same but the winning rule or reason
1545	        differs; identical results only count as ``unchanged``. The three
1546	        change kinds are disjoint, so ``changed`` is always their sum.
1547	
1548	        The comparison is read-only and offline: neither gate, request
1549	        mapping nor tag mapping is modified, no I/O happens, and repeated
1550	        calls return equal results.
1551	        """
1552	        if not isinstance(candidate, PolicyGate):
1553	            raise TypeError("candidate must be a PolicyGate instance")
1554	        self._validate_requests(requests)
1555	
1556	        changes = []
1557	        allow_to_deny = deny_to_allow = winner_changed = 0
1558	        for index, item in enumerate(requests):
1559	            before = self.decide(
1560	                item["subject"],
1561	                item["action"],
1562	                item["resource"],
1563	                item.get("tags"),
1564	            )
1565	            after = candidate.decide(
1566	                item["subject"],
1567	                item["action"],
1568	                item["resource"],
1569	                item.get("tags"),
1570	            )
1571	            if before == after:
1572	                continue
1573	            if before["effect"] != after["effect"]:
1574	                if after["effect"] == "deny":
1575	                    kind = "allow_to_deny"
1576	                    allow_to_deny += 1
1577	                else:
1578	                    kind = "deny_to_allow"
1579	                    deny_to_allow += 1
1580	            else:
1581	                kind = "winner_changed"
1582	                winner_changed += 1
1583	            changes.append(
1584	                {"index": index, "before": before, "after": after, "kind": kind}
1585	            )
1586	
1587	        changed = allow_to_deny + deny_to_allow + winner_changed
1588	        summary = {
1589	            "total": len(requests),
1590	            "unchanged": len(requests) - changed,
1591	            "changed": changed,
1592	            "allow_to_deny": allow_to_deny,
1593	            "deny_to_allow": deny_to_allow,
1594	            "winner_changed": winner_changed,
1595	        }
1596	        return {"changes": changes, "summary": summary}

1608	            {"id": r["id"], "effect": r["effect"], "priority": r["priority"]}
1609	            for r in matched

1613	    def trace(self, subject, action, resource, tags=None):
1614	        """Per-rule decision trace of one request, for offline review.

1619	        rule in declaration order, each with the fixed key order ``id``,

1636	        deny (``rule`` is then ``None``).

1639	        modified and no I/O happens.

1714	        list; it only analyzes the rules that loaded successfully, so
1715	        decide()/explain()/decide_many() results are unaffected.

1717	        Every pair of rules is checked in declaration order. Two
1718	        selectors overlap when some subject/action/resource string
1719	        matches both glob patterns under fnmatch.fnmatchcase semantics
1720	        and their tag constraints are jointly satisfiable (a shared tag
1721	        key with different exact values conflicts; an exact value must
1722	        match a shared key's ``tag_patterns`` pattern; two patterns on a
1723	        shared key need one common string; extra caller tags do not
1724	        matter) and, for every key constrained by either rule, some tag
1725	        value satisfies both sides' positive constraints while matching
1726	        none of their ``tag_exclude_patterns`` exclusion patterns (an
1727	        exact value must avoid them too), and their ``tag_presence``
1728	        presence constraints are jointly satisfiable (one rule requiring
1729	        a key the other forbids, or a forbidden key pinned by an exact
1730	        or pattern constraint, makes the pair unsatisfiable). Overlapping selectors with
1731	        different effects yield one
1732	        ``effect_overlap`` error finding whose winner is the deny rule —
1733	        explicit deny overrides allow, and priority cannot change that.
1734	        Selectors with identical pattern texts, tags and exclusion
1735	        patterns yield one
1736	        ``shadowed_rule`` finding instead: an error when deny shadows
1737	        allow, a warning when same-effect rules collide (the loser by
1738	        priority, then declaration order, is shadowed). Same-effect
1739	        partial overlaps are not conflicts and produce no finding.

1744	        ``reason`` and ``witness``; ``rule``/``other_rule`` are the
1745	        earlier/later declared rule ids and ``shadowed`` is None when no
1746	        rule is fully shadowed. Findings are stably ordered by declaration
1747	        position with at most one finding per pair. With no overlapping
1748	        selectors the report is empty and every summary count is 0.

805	    def assertWitnessTriggers(self, gate, finding):
806	        witness = finding["witness"]
807	        self.assertEqual(
808	            set(witness), {"subject", "action", "resource", "tags"}
809	        )
810	        rules = {r["id"]: r for r in gate.rules}
811	        for rid in (finding["rule"], finding["other_rule"]):
812	            self.assertTrue(

816	                    witness["action"],
817	                    witness["resource"],

820	                "witness %r does not match rule %r of finding %r"
821	                % (witness, rid, finding["code"]),
822	            )
823	        explanation = gate.explain(
824	            witness["subject"],
825	            witness["action"],
826	            witness["resource"],
827	            witness["tags"],
828	        )
829	        matched_ids = [m["id"] for m in explanation["matched_rules"]]
830	        self.assertIn(finding["rule"], matched_ids)
831	        self.assertIn(finding["other_rule"], matched_ids)
832	        # pairwise replay: with only the pair present, the named winner
833	        # must win exactly as the finding describes
834	        pair_decision, pair_winner = PolicyGate._select(
835	            [rules[finding["rule"]], rules[finding["other_rule"]]]
836	        )

838	        if finding["code"] == "effect_overlap":
839	            self.assertEqual(pair_decision["effect"], "deny")
840	            # the deny side can never be overridden globally either
841	            self.assertEqual(explanation["effect"], "deny")
842	        elif finding["severity"] == "error":

import unittest

from app import PolicyBatchError, PolicyConfigError, PolicyGate, PolicyVerificationError


class BackwardCompatTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_default_deny_shape(self):
        gate = PolicyGate([])
        result = gate.decide("alice", "read", "data/x")
        self.assertEqual(result["effect"], "deny")
        self.assertIsNone(result["rule"])
        self.assertEqual(result["reason"], "default deny")

    def test_legacy_fnmatch_and_tags(self):
        gate = PolicyGate(
            [
                {"effect": "allow", "action": "read", "resource": "docs/*"},
                {"id": "tagged", "effect": "allow", "tags": {"env": "prod"}},
            ]
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            gate.decide("bob", "read", "docs/a", {"env": "dev"})["rule"], "0"
        )
        # tags are a key/value subset match; extra caller tags are fine
        self.assertEqual(
            gate.decide("bob", "write", "x", {"env": "prod", "x": 1})["rule"],
            "tagged",
        )
        # fnmatch is case sensitive
        self.assertEqual(
            gate.decide("bob", "READ", "docs/a")["effect"], "deny"
        )

    def test_missing_tag_value_does_not_match(self):
        gate = PolicyGate([{"id": "a", "effect": "allow", "tags": {"k": "v"}}])
        self.assertEqual(gate.decide("s", "a", "r")["effect"], "deny")

    def test_demo_gate(self):
        gate = PolicyGate(
            [
                {"id": "read", "effect": "allow", "action": "read"},
                {"id": "prod-lock", "effect": "deny", "resource": "prod/*"},
            ]
        )
        self.assertEqual(gate.decide("alice", "read", "prod/db")["effect"], "deny")
        self.assertEqual(gate.decide("alice", "read", "dev/db")["effect"], "allow")


class PriorityAndConflictTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_explicit_deny_beats_higher_priority_allow(self):
        gate = PolicyGate(
            [
                {"id": "a1", "effect": "allow", "priority": 100},
                {"id": "d1", "effect": "deny", "priority": -5},
            ]
        )
        result = gate.decide("s", "a", "r")
        self.assertEqual(result["effect"], "deny")
        self.assertEqual(result["rule"], "d1")
        self.assertIn("deny", result["reason"])
        self.assertIn("d1", result["reason"])
        self.assertIn("priority", result["reason"])
        self.assertIn("overrides allow", result["reason"])

    def test_higher_priority_allow_wins(self):
        gate = PolicyGate(
            [
                {"id": "low", "effect": "allow", "priority": 1},
                {"id": "high", "effect": "allow", "priority": 10},
            ]
        )
        result = gate.decide("s", "a", "r")
        self.assertEqual(result["effect"], "allow")
        self.assertEqual(result["rule"], "high")

    def test_equal_priority_keeps_declaration_order(self):
        gate = PolicyGate(
            [
                {"id": "first", "effect": "allow"},
                {"id": "second", "effect": "allow"},
            ]
        )
        self.assertEqual(gate.decide("s", "a", "r")["rule"], "first")

    def test_deny_tie_keeps_declaration_order(self):
        gate = PolicyGate(
            [
                {"id": "d-first", "effect": "deny", "priority": 5},
                {"id": "d-second", "effect": "deny", "priority": 5},
                {"id": "a", "effect": "allow", "priority": 9},
            ]
        )
        self.assertEqual(gate.decide("s", "a", "r")["rule"], "d-first")

    def test_decision_is_deterministic(self):
        gate = PolicyGate(
            [
                {"id": "a1", "effect": "allow", "priority": 1},
                {"id": "a2", "effect": "allow", "priority": 2},
                {"id": "d1", "effect": "deny", "priority": 1},
                {"id": "d2", "effect": "deny", "priority": 2},
            ]
        )
        results = [gate.decide("s", "a", "r") for _ in range(20)]
        self.assertTrue(all(r == results[0] for r in results))
        self.assertEqual(results[0]["rule"], "d2")

    def test_reason_mentions_effect_id_priority(self):
        gate = PolicyGate([{"id": "x", "effect": "allow", "priority": 7}])
        reason = gate.decide("s", "a", "r")["reason"]
        self.assertIn("allow", reason)
        self.assertIn("x", reason)
        self.assertIn("7", reason)

    def test_default_priority_is_zero(self):
        gate = PolicyGate([{"id": "x", "effect": "allow"}])
        self.assertIn("priority 0", gate.decide("s", "a", "r")["reason"])


class LoadValidationTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def _expect_value_error(self, rules):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            PolicyGate(rules)

    def test_non_mapping_rule(self):
        self._expect_value_error([["not", "a", "dict"]])

    def test_bad_effect(self):
        self._expect_value_error([{"id": "x", "effect": "maybe"}])

    def test_missing_effect(self):
        self._expect_value_error([{"id": "x"}])

    def test_empty_and_non_string_id(self):
        self._expect_value_error([{"id": "", "effect": "allow"}])
        self._expect_value_error([{"id": 3, "effect": "allow"}])

    def test_duplicate_ids(self):
        self._expect_value_error(
            [
                {"id": "x", "effect": "allow"},
                {"id": "x", "effect": "deny"},
            ]
        )

    def test_duplicate_default_and_explicit_id(self):
        self._expect_value_error(
            [
                {"id": "1", "effect": "allow"},
                {"effect": "deny"},
            ]
        )

    def test_bad_priority(self):
        self._expect_value_error([{"id": "x", "effect": "allow", "priority": 1.5}])
        self._expect_value_error([{"id": "x", "effect": "allow", "priority": True}])
        self._expect_value_error([{"id": "x", "effect": "allow", "priority": "1"}])

    def test_bad_string_fields(self):
        self._expect_value_error([{"id": "x", "effect": "allow", "subject": 1}])
        self._expect_value_error([{"id": "x", "effect": "allow", "action": None}])

class ExplainTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def _gate(self):
        return PolicyGate(
            [
                {"id": "r-low", "effect": "allow", "priority": -1, "action": "read"},
                {"id": "r-high", "effect": "allow", "priority": 10, "action": "read"},
                {"id": "w-star", "effect": "allow", "action": "*", "tags": {"env": "dev"}},
                {"id": "d-prod", "effect": "deny", "resource": "prod/*"},
                {"id": "d-other", "effect": "deny", "action": "write"},
                {"id": "miss", "effect": "allow", "subject": "nobody"},
            ]
        )

    def test_core_fields_equal_decide(self):
        gate = self._gate()
        for args in (
            ("alice", "read", "dev/x", None),
            ("alice", "read", "prod/db", {"env": "dev"}),
            ("bob", "write", "x", {"env": "dev"}),
            ("bob", "delete", "x", {"env": "prod"}),
        ):
            decision = gate.decide(*args)
            explanation = gate.explain(*args)
            for key in ("effect", "rule", "reason"):
                self.assertEqual(explanation[key], decision[key])

    def test_matched_rules_in_declaration_order(self):
        gate = self._gate()
        explanation = gate.explain("alice", "read", "dev/x", {"env": "dev"})
        self.assertEqual(explanation["rule"], "r-high")
        self.assertEqual(
            explanation["matched_rules"],
            [
                {"id": "r-low", "effect": "allow", "priority": -1},
                {"id": "r-high", "effect": "allow", "priority": 10},
                {"id": "w-star", "effect": "allow", "priority": 0},
            ],
        )

    def test_deny_and_allow_both_listed(self):
        gate = self._gate()
        explanation = gate.explain("alice", "read", "prod/db", {"env": "dev"})
        self.assertEqual(explanation["effect"], "deny")
        self.assertEqual(explanation["rule"], "d-prod")
        self.assertIn("overrides allow", explanation["reason"])
        self.assertEqual(
            explanation["matched_rules"],
            [
                {"id": "r-low", "effect": "allow", "priority": -1},
                {"id": "r-high", "effect": "allow", "priority": 10},
                {"id": "w-star", "effect": "allow", "priority": 0},
                {"id": "d-prod", "effect": "deny", "priority": 0},
            ],
        )

    def test_unmatched_rules_never_listed(self):
        gate = PolicyGate(
            [
                {"id": "a", "effect": "allow", "subject": "alice"},
                {"id": "b", "effect": "deny", "subject": "bob"},
            ]
        )
        explanation = gate.explain("carol", "x", "y")
        self.assertEqual(explanation["matched_rules"], [])

    def test_default_deny_shape(self):
        gate = PolicyGate([])
        explanation = gate.explain("s", "a", "r")
        self.assertEqual(explanation["effect"], "deny")
        self.assertIsNone(explanation["rule"])
        self.assertEqual(explanation["reason"], "default deny")
        self.assertEqual(explanation["matched_rules"], [])

    def test_equal_priority_uses_declaration_order(self):
        gate = PolicyGate(
            [
                {"id": "first", "effect": "allow", "priority": 2},
                {"id": "second", "effect": "allow", "priority": 2},
            ]
        )
        explanation = gate.explain("s", "a", "r")
        self.assertEqual(explanation["rule"], "first")
        self.assertEqual(
            explanation["matched_rules"],
            [
                {"id": "first", "effect": "allow", "priority": 2},
                {"id": "second", "effect": "allow", "priority": 2},
            ],
        )

    def test_type_errors_match_decide(self):
        gate = PolicyGate([{"id": "x", "effect": "allow"}])
        for bad in ((1, "a", "r"), ("s", ["a"], "r"), ("s", "a", None)):
            with self.assertRaises(TypeError) as d_ctx:
                gate.decide(*bad)
            with self.assertRaises(TypeError) as e_ctx:
                gate.explain(*bad)
            self.assertEqual(str(e_ctx.exception), str(d_ctx.exception))
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError) as d_ctx:
            gate.decide("s", "a", "r", tags="k=v")
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError) as e_ctx:
            gate.explain("s", "a", "r", tags="k=v")
        self.assertEqual(str(e_ctx.exception), str(d_ctx.exception))

    def test_tags_none_treated_as_empty(self):
        gate = PolicyGate([{"id": "x", "effect": "allow"}])
        explanation = gate.explain("s", "a", "r", tags=None)
        self.assertEqual(explanation["effect"], "allow")
        self.assertEqual(
            explanation["matched_rules"],
            [{"id": "x", "effect": "allow", "priority": 0}],
        )

    def test_repeatable_and_read_only(self):
        gate = self._gate()
        before = [dict(r) for r in gate.rules]
        first = gate.explain("alice", "read", "prod/db", {"env": "dev"})
        for _ in range(20):
            again = gate.explain("alice", "read", "prod/db", {"env": "dev"})
            self.assertEqual(again, first)
        self.assertEqual(gate.rules, before)
        # returned entries must not alias internal rule mappings
        first["matched_rules"].append({"id": "tampered", "effect": "deny", "priority": 0})
        self.assertEqual(
            gate.explain("alice", "read", "prod/db", {"env": "dev"})["matched_rules"],
            first["matched_rules"][:-1],
        )


class FromJsonTest(unittest.TestCase):
    DOCUMENT = (
        '['
        '{"id": "read", "effect": "allow", "action": "read", "resource": "docs/*"},'

        '{"id": "num", "effect": "allow", "priority": 5}'
        ']'

    def test_loads_and_decides_like_constructor(self):
        gate = PolicyGate.from_json(self.DOCUMENT)
        legacy = PolicyGate(
            [
                {"id": "read", "effect": "allow", "action": "read", "resource": "docs/*"},
                {"effect": "deny", "resource": "secret/*", "tags": {"env": "prod"}},
                {"id": "num", "effect": "allow", "priority": 5},
            ]
        )
        for args in (
            ("alice", "read", "docs/a", None),
            ("alice", "read", "secret/x", None),
            ("bob", "write", "x", {"env": "prod"}),
            ("bob", "write", "x", {"env": "dev"}),
        ):
            self.assertEqual(gate.decide(*args), legacy.decide(*args))
            self.assertEqual(gate.explain(*args), legacy.explain(*args))

    def test_defaults_are_applied(self):
        gate = PolicyGate.from_json('[{"effect": "allow"}]')
        self.assertEqual(gate.rules[0]["id"], "0")
        self.assertEqual(gate.rules[0]["priority"], 0)
        self.assertEqual(gate.rules[0]["subject"], "*")
        self.assertEqual(gate.rules[0]["action"], "*")
        self.assertEqual(gate.rules[0]["resource"], "*")
        self.assertEqual(gate.rules[0]["tags"], {})

    def test_empty_array_is_default_deny(self):
        gate = PolicyGate.from_json("[]")
        self.assertEqual(gate.rules, [])
        result = gate.decide("s", "a", "r")
        self.assertEqual(result["effect"], "deny")
        self.assertIsNone(result["rule"])
        self.assertEqual(result["reason"], "default deny")

    def test_whitespace_only_wrapping_is_fine(self):
        gate = PolicyGate.from_json('  \n\t [ ] \t\n  ')
        self.assertEqual(gate.decide("s", "a", "r")["effect"], "deny")

    def test_case_sensitive_fnmatch_preserved(self):
        gate = PolicyGate.from_json(
            '[{"id": "a", "effect": "allow", "action": "read"}]'
        )
        self.assertEqual(gate.decide("s", "read", "r")["effect"], "allow")
        self.assertEqual(gate.decide("s", "READ", "r")["effect"], "deny")

    def test_explicit_deny_and_priority_semantics_preserved(self):
        gate = PolicyGate.from_json(
            '['
            '{"id": "a", "effect": "allow", "priority": 100},'
            '{"id": "d", "effect": "deny", "priority": -5}'
            ']'
        )
        result = gate.decide("s", "a", "r")
        self.assertEqual(result["effect"], "deny")
        self.assertEqual(result["rule"], "d")

    # --- input type -------------------------------------------------

    def test_non_string_document_raises_type_error(self):
        for bad in (None, 1, 1.5, b"[]", [], {}, True):
            with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
                PolicyGate.from_json(bad)

    def test_bytes_are_not_silently_decoded(self):
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            PolicyGate.from_json(b'[{"effect": "allow"}]')

    # --- structural errors ------------------------------------------

    def _expect_code(self, document, code):
        with self.assertRaises(PolicyConfigError) as ctx:
            PolicyGate.from_json(document)
        self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.code, code)
        self.assertIn(code, str(ctx.exception))

    def test_invalid_json_syntax(self):
        for bad in ("", "   ", "{", "[{", "[,]", "not json", "[1,]"):
            self._expect_code(bad, "invalid_json")

    def test_non_finite_numbers_are_invalid_json(self):
        self._expect_code("[NaN]", "invalid_json")
        self._expect_code("[Infinity]", "invalid_json")
        self._expect_code("[-Infinity]", "invalid_json")

    def test_duplicate_key_at_rule_level(self):
        self._expect_code(
            '[{"id": "x", "id": "y", "effect": "allow"}]', "duplicate_key"
        )

    def test_duplicate_key_nested_in_tags(self):
        self._expect_code(
            '[{"effect": "allow", "tags": {"k": "a", "k": "b"}}]',
            "duplicate_key",
        )

    def test_root_not_array(self):
        for bad in ('{"effect": "allow"}', "5", '"str"', "true", "null"):
            self._expect_code(bad, "root_not_array")

    def test_rule_not_object_reports_index(self):
        with self.assertRaises(PolicyConfigError) as ctx:
            PolicyGate.from_json('[{"effect": "allow"}, 5]')
        self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.code, "rule_not_object")
        self.assertIn("rule 1", str(ctx.exception))
        for bad in ("[[]]", '["allow"]', "[true]", "[null]"):
            self._expect_code(bad, "rule_not_object")

    def test_first_bad_element_index_is_reported(self):
        with self.assertRaises(PolicyConfigError) as ctx:
            PolicyGate.from_json('["nope", {"effect": "allow"}]')
        self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.code, "rule_not_object")
        self.assertIn("rule 0", str(ctx.exception))

    # --- semantic errors reuse ValueError ---------------------------

    def _expect_value_error(self, document):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as ctx:
            PolicyGate.from_json(document)
        self.assertNotIsInstance(ctx.exception, PolicyConfigError)
        return ctx

    def test_missing_effect_is_value_error(self):
        self._expect_value_error('[{"id": "x"}]')

    def test_unknown_field_is_value_error(self):
        ctx = self._expect_value_error(
            '[{"id": "x", "effect": "allow", "bogus": 1}]'
        )
        self.assertIn("rule 0", str(ctx.exception))

    def test_duplicate_id_is_value_error(self):
        self._expect_value_error(
            '[{"id": "x", "effect": "allow"},'
            '{"id": "x", "effect": "deny"}]'
        )

    def test_type_mismatches_are_value_errors(self):
        self._expect_value_error('[{"id": "x", "effect": "allow", "priority": 1.5}]')
        self._expect_value_error('[{"id": "x", "effect": "allow", "priority": "1"}]')
        self._expect_value_error('[{"id": 3, "effect": "allow"}]')
        self._expect_value_error('[{"effect": "allow", "subject": 1}]')
        self._expect_value_error('[{"effect": "allow", "tags": []}]')

    def test_semantic_error_names_first_offending_index(self):
        ctx = self._expect_value_error(
            '['
            '{"id": "ok", "effect": "allow"},'
            '{"id": "bad", "effect": "allow", "priority": "nope"},'
            '{"id": "also", "effect": "wat"}'
            ']'
        )
        self.assertIn("rule 1", str(ctx.exception))
        self.assertIn("priority", str(ctx.exception))

    # --- no side effects / no half-built instance -------------------

    def test_failed_load_leaves_no_instance(self):
        with self.assertRaises(PolicyConfigError):
            PolicyGate.from_json('[{"effect": "allow"}, oops]')
        with self.assertRaises(PolicyConfigError):
            PolicyGate.from_json('{"effect": "allow"}')
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            PolicyGate.from_json('[{"id": "x"}]')

    def test_input_text_is_not_mutated(self):
        document = '[{"effect": "allow"}]'
        snapshot = document
        PolicyGate.from_json(document)
        self.assertEqual(document, snapshot)
        self.assertIs(document, snapshot)

    def test_loaded_decisions_match_after_text_is_reused(self):
        document = '[{"id": "x", "effect": "allow"}]'
        gate = PolicyGate.from_json(document)
        again = PolicyGate.from_json(document)
        self.assertEqual(
            gate.decide("s", "a", "r"), again.decide("s", "a", "r")
        )


class AuditTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_empty_rules_empty_report(self):
        self.assertEqual(
            PolicyGate([]).audit(),
            {"findings": [], "summary": {"total": 0, "error": 0, "warning": 0}},
        )

    def test_no_overlap_empty_report(self):
        gate = PolicyGate(
            [
                {"id": "a", "effect": "allow", "subject": "alice"},
                {"id": "d", "effect": "deny", "subject": "bob"},
            ]
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            gate.audit(),
            {"findings": [], "summary": {"total": 0, "error": 0, "warning": 0}},
        )

    def test_similar_but_disjoint_patterns_not_flagged(self):
        disjoint_pairs = [
            ("data/[0-9]*", "data/[a-z]*"),
            ("a*", "b*"),
            ("[!a]", "a"),
            ("prod/?", "prod/xy"),
            ("[z-a]", "*"),  # empty range never matches anything
        ]
        for first, second in disjoint_pairs:
            gate = PolicyGate(
                [
                    {"id": "a", "effect": "allow", "resource": first},
                    {"id": "d", "effect": "deny", "resource": second},
                ]
            )
            self.assertEqual(
                gate.audit()["findings"],
                [],
                "patterns %r and %r must not be reported as overlapping"
                % (first, second),
            )

    def test_effect_overlap_error(self):
        gate = PolicyGate(
            [
                {"id": "a1", "effect": "allow", "resource": "data/*"},
                {"id": "d1", "effect": "deny", "resource": "data/secret*"},
            ]
        )
        report = gate.audit()
        self.assertEqual(report["summary"], {"total": 1, "error": 1, "warning": 0})
        (finding,) = report["findings"]
        self.assertEqual(
            finding,
            {
                "code": "effect_overlap",
                "severity": "error",
                "rule": "a1",
                "other_rule": "d1",
                "winner": "d1",
                "shadowed": None,
                "reason": finding["reason"],
                "witness": finding["witness"],
            },
        )
        self.assertIn("deny", finding["reason"])
        self.assertIn("allow", finding["reason"])

    def test_effect_overlap_winner_ignores_priority(self):
        gate = PolicyGate(
            [
                {"id": "d1", "effect": "deny", "priority": -5, "action": "read"},
                {"id": "a1", "effect": "allow", "priority": 100, "action": "r*"},
            ]
        )
        (finding,) = gate.audit()["findings"]
        self.assertEqual(finding["code"], "effect_overlap")
        # rule/other_rule follow declaration order, not effect or priority
        self.assertEqual(finding["rule"], "d1")
        self.assertEqual(finding["other_rule"], "a1")
        self.assertEqual(finding["winner"], "d1")
        self.assertIsNone(finding["shadowed"])

    def test_shadowed_allow_by_deny_is_error(self):
        gate = PolicyGate(
            [
                {"id": "a1", "effect": "allow", "priority": 10, "action": "read"},
                {"id": "d1", "effect": "deny", "priority": -1, "action": "read"},
            ]
        )
        (finding,) = gate.audit()["findings"]
        self.assertEqual(finding["code"], "shadowed_rule")
        self.assertEqual(finding["severity"], "error")
        self.assertEqual(finding["winner"], "d1")
        self.assertEqual(finding["shadowed"], "a1")

    def test_shadowed_same_effect_is_warning(self):
        gate = PolicyGate(
            [
                {"id": "first", "effect": "allow", "action": "read"},
                {"id": "second", "effect": "allow", "action": "read"},
            ]
        )
        (finding,) = gate.audit()["findings"]
        self.assertEqual(finding["code"], "shadowed_rule")
        self.assertEqual(finding["severity"], "warning")
        self.assertEqual(finding["winner"], "first")
        self.assertEqual(finding["shadowed"], "second")

    def test_shadowed_same_effect_uses_priority(self):
        gate = PolicyGate(
            [
                {"id": "low", "effect": "deny", "priority": 1},
                {"id": "high", "effect": "deny", "priority": 9},
            ]
        )
        (finding,) = gate.audit()["findings"]
        self.assertEqual(finding["severity"], "warning")
        self.assertEqual(finding["winner"], "high")
        self.assertEqual(finding["shadowed"], "low")

    def test_same_effect_partial_overlap_no_finding(self):
        gate = PolicyGate(
            [
                {"id": "a", "effect": "allow", "resource": "data/*"},
                {"id": "b", "effect": "allow", "resource": "data/x*"},
                {"id": "c", "effect": "deny", "resource": "a*"},
                {"id": "d", "effect": "deny", "resource": "ab*"},
            ]
        )
        self.assertEqual(gate.audit()["findings"], [])

    def test_tag_conflict_prevents_overlap(self):
        gate = PolicyGate(
            [
                {"id": "a", "effect": "allow", "tags": {"env": "prod"}},
                {"id": "d", "effect": "deny", "tags": {"env": "dev"}},
            ]
        )
        self.assertEqual(gate.audit()["findings"], [])

    def test_disjoint_tag_keys_still_overlap(self):
        gate = PolicyGate(
            [
                {"id": "a", "effect": "allow", "tags": {"env": "prod"}},
                {"id": "d", "effect": "deny", "tags": {"team": "sec"}},
            ]
        )
        (finding,) = gate.audit()["findings"]
        self.assertEqual(finding["code"], "effect_overlap")

    def test_glob_semantics_in_overlap(self):
        # 'a?c' and 'abc' both match "abc"; '?' and '[!x]' share characters
        for first, second in (("a?c", "abc"), ("?", "[!x]"), ("a*", "*b")):
            gate = PolicyGate(
                [
                    {"id": "a", "effect": "allow", "action": first},
                    {"id": "d", "effect": "deny", "action": second},
                ]
            )
            (finding,) = gate.audit()["findings"]
            self.assertEqual(finding["code"], "effect_overlap")

    def test_summary_counts_and_stable_order(self):
        gate = PolicyGate(
            [
                {"id": "r0", "effect": "allow", "action": "read"},
                {"id": "r1", "effect": "deny", "action": "r*"},
                {"id": "r2", "effect": "allow", "action": "read"},
                {"id": "r3", "effect": "deny", "resource": "x"},
                {"id": "r4", "effect": "deny", "resource": "x"},
            ]
        )
        report = gate.audit()
        pairs = [(f["rule"], f["other_rule"]) for f in report["findings"]]
        self.assertEqual(pairs, sorted(pairs))
        self.assertEqual(len(pairs), len(set(pairs)))
        self.assertEqual(
            report["summary"],
            {
                "total": len(report["findings"]),
                "error": sum(
                    1 for f in report["findings"] if f["severity"] == "error"
                ),
                "warning": sum(
                    1 for f in report["findings"] if f["severity"] == "warning"
                ),
            },
        )
        self.assertGreater(report["summary"]["error"], 0)
        self.assertGreater(report["summary"]["warning"], 0)

    def test_audit_is_read_only_and_decisions_unchanged(self):
        rules = [
            {"id": "a1", "effect": "allow", "priority": 5, "resource": "data/*"},
            {"id": "d1", "effect": "deny", "resource": "data/secret*"},
            {"id": "a2", "effect": "allow", "resource": "data/*"},
        ]
        gate = PolicyGate(rules)
        before = [dict(r) for r in gate.rules]
        decisions_before = gate.decide_many(
            [
                {"subject": "s", "action": "read", "resource": "data/x"},
                {"subject": "s", "action": "read", "resource": "data/secret1"},
            ]
        )
        first = gate.audit()
        for _ in range(5):
            self.assertEqual(gate.audit(), first)
        self.assertEqual(gate.rules, before)
        self.assertEqual(
            gate.decide_many(
                [
                    {"subject": "s", "action": "read", "resource": "data/x"},
                    {"subject": "s", "action": "read", "resource": "data/secret1"},
                ]
            ),
            decisions_before,
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            gate.decide("s", "read", "data/x"),
            {"effect": "allow", "rule": "a1",
             "reason": "matched allow rule 'a1' (priority 5)"},
        )

    def test_audit_matches_from_json_gate(self):
        document = (
            '[{"id": "read", "effect": "allow", "action": "read"},'
            '{"effect": "deny", "resource": "secret/*", "tags": {"env": "prod"}}]'
        )
        gate = PolicyGate.from_json(document)
        legacy = PolicyGate(
            [
                {"id": "read", "effect": "allow", "action": "read"},
                {"effect": "deny", "resource": "secret/*", "tags": {"env": "prod"}},
            ]
        )
        self.assertEqual(gate.audit(), legacy.audit())
        # read-anything allow vs secret/* prod deny overlap on e.g. a

class WitnessTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def _gate_for_pair(self, first, second):
        return PolicyGate(
            [
                dict(first, id="r1"),
                dict(second, id="r2"),
            ]
        )

    def assertWitnessTriggers(self, gate, finding):
        witness = finding["witness"]
        self.assertEqual(
            set(witness), {"subject", "action", "resource", "tags"}
        )
        rules = {r["id"]: r for r in gate.rules}
        for rid in (finding["rule"], finding["other_rule"]):
            self.assertTrue(
                PolicyGate._matches(
                    rules[rid],
                    witness["subject"],
                    witness["action"],
                    witness["resource"],
                    witness["tags"],
                ),
                "witness %r does not match rule %r of finding %r"
                % (witness, rid, finding["code"]),
            )
        explanation = gate.explain(
            witness["subject"],
            witness["action"],
            witness["resource"],
            witness["tags"],
        )
        matched_ids = [m["id"] for m in explanation["matched_rules"]]
        self.assertIn(finding["rule"], matched_ids)
        self.assertIn(finding["other_rule"], matched_ids)
        # pairwise replay: with only the pair present, the named winner
        # must win exactly as the finding describes
        pair_decision, pair_winner = PolicyGate._select(
            [rules[finding["rule"]], rules[finding["other_rule"]]]
        )
        self.assertEqual(pair_winner["id"], finding["winner"])
        if finding["code"] == "effect_overlap":
            self.assertEqual(pair_decision["effect"], "deny")
            # the deny side can never be overridden globally either
            self.assertEqual(explanation["effect"], "deny")
        elif finding["severity"] == "error":
            self.assertEqual(pair_decision["effect"], "deny")
        return explanation

        for finding in report["findings"]:
            self.assertIn(
                "witness", finding, "finding %r has no witness" % finding
            )
            explanation = self.assertWitnessTriggers(gate, finding)
            if finding["code"] == "effect_overlap":
                # explicit deny cannot be undone by any third rule either

    def test_full_gate_random_witness_fuzz(self):
        import fnmatch
        import random

        random.seed(99)
        alphabet = list("ab[]*?!x-中")
        tag_values = ("v1", "v2")
        for _ in range(150):
            rules = []
            for idx in range(random.randint(2, 6)):
                rule = {
                    "id": "r%d" % idx,
                    "effect": random.choice(("allow", "deny")),
                    "priority": random.randint(0, 3),
                }
                for field in ("subject", "action", "resource"):
                    if random.random() < 0.8:
                        rule[field] = "".join(
                            random.choice(alphabet)
                            for _ in range(random.randint(0, 5))
                        )
                tags = {}
                for key in ("env", "team", "中"):
                    if random.random() < 0.5:
                        tags[key] = random.choice(tag_values)
                rule["tags"] = tags
                rules.append(rule)
            gate = PolicyGate(rules)
            by_id = {r["id"]: r for r in gate.rules}
            report = gate.audit()
            seen_pairs = set()
            for finding in report["findings"]:
                pair = (finding["rule"], finding["other_rule"])
                self.assertEqual(len(pair), len(set(pair)))
                self.assertNotIn(pair, seen_pairs)
                seen_pairs.add(pair)
                self.assertEqual(
                    set(finding),
                    {
                        "code", "severity", "rule", "other_rule", "winner",
                        "shadowed", "reason", "witness",
                    },
                )
                w = finding["witness"]
                self.assertEqual(
                    set(w), {"subject", "action", "resource", "tags"}
                )
                for rid in pair:
                    r = by_id[rid]
                    self.assertTrue(fnmatch.fnmatchcase(w["subject"], r["subject"]))
                    self.assertTrue(fnmatch.fnmatchcase(w["action"], r["action"]))
                    self.assertTrue(
                        fnmatch.fnmatchcase(w["resource"], r["resource"])
                    )
                    for key, value in r["tags"].items():
                        self.assertEqual(w["tags"][key], value)
                # no invented tags: witness tags are exactly the union
                union_keys = set(by_id[pair[0]]["tags"]) | set(
                    by_id[pair[1]]["tags"]
                )
                self.assertEqual(set(w["tags"]), union_keys)
                # deny on the pair is always the winner of an overlap
                if finding["code"] == "effect_overlap":
                    self.assertEqual(
                        by_id[finding["winner"]]["effect"], "deny"
                    )
            # repeatability under the same rules
            self.assertEqual(gate.audit(), report)


def _min_common_from_patterns(first, second):
    from app import _tokenize_pattern, _min_common_string

    return _min_common_string(
        _tokenize_pattern(first), _tokenize_pattern(second)
    )

        self.assertEqual(reloaded.audit(), gate.audit())

        )

        self.candidate = PolicyGate(
            [

                {"id": "prod-lock", "effect": "deny", "resource": "prod/*"},

            report["summary"],
